topics.title: Ecosystems, food chains and energy flow

learn.hook: In the Sundarbans, a tiger's dinner depends on deer, which depend on grass, which depends on the Sun — everything is connected!
points: An ecosystem is made of all living things (biotic components) in an area together with non-living (abiotic) factors such as temperature, rainfall, wind and soil. Forests, ponds and lakes are natural ecosystems; gardens, crop fields and aquariums are artificial ones.

Producers (green plants and blue-green algae) make food by photosynthesis. Consumers eat others: herbivores, carnivores, omnivores and parasites. Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead remains and return nutrients to the soil.

A food chain shows who eats whom, e.g. grass → deer → lion. Each step is a trophic level: producers (1st), herbivores or primary consumers (2nd), small carnivores or secondary consumers (3rd), large carnivores or tertiary consumers (4th). Food chains interlink to form food webs.

Green plants capture only about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves. The 10 percent law: only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next; the rest is used for life processes or lost as heat.
So energy flow is unidirectional (it never returns to the Sun or to the plants), food chains usually have only three or four steps, and there are fewer organisms at higher trophic levels.

example.q: In a food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, the grass traps 10,000 J of energy. How much energy reaches the snake?
steps: By the 10 percent law, each level passes on about 10%.
Grasshopper: 10% of 10,000 J = 1000 J.
Snake: 10% of 100 J = 10 J.

learn.reallife: In a farm pond in a village, algae feed tiny animals, which feed small fish, which feed larger fish and kingfishers — a complete aquatic food chain.

quiz.q: Which of these is an artificial ecosystem?
quiz.explain: Crop fields, gardens and aquariums are made and maintained by humans.
steps: Natural ecosystems: forests, ponds, lakes.
Artificial ecosystems are made and maintained by humans: gardens, crop fields, aquariums.
So a crop field is an artificial ecosystem.
Answer: A crop field
quiz.mistake: Thinks any ecosystem with water is natural only

quiz.q: Grass → deer → lion. At which trophic level is the lion?
quiz.explain: Grass (producer) is first, deer (herbivore) second and lion (carnivore) third.
steps: Grass is a producer → 1st trophic level.
Deer is a herbivore → 2nd level.
Lion eats the deer → 3rd level.
Answer: Third
quiz.mistake: Counts the lion as the first level

quiz.q: According to the 10 percent law, if producers have 10,000 J of energy, how much (in joules) reaches the primary consumers?
quiz.explain: About 10% of 10,000 J = 1000 J is passed on to the herbivores.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 10% instead of keeping 10%
steps: Answer: 1000

quiz.q: What is the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
options: They break down dead remains and return nutrients to the soil
quiz.explain: Bacteria and fungi break complex organic matter into simple substances that plants reuse.
steps: Decomposers are bacteria and fungi.
They break down dead remains into simple substances.
These nutrients return to the soil for plants to reuse.
Answer: They break down dead remains and return nutrients to the soil
quiz.mistake: Confuses decomposers with producers

quiz.q: Why are food chains generally limited to three or four steps?
options: Animals do not like long chains
So much energy is lost at each level that little is left for higher levels
quiz.explain: Only about 10% of energy passes on each time, so after a few steps too little remains to support another level.
steps: Only about 10% of energy passes from one level to the next.
After a few steps very little energy is left.
Too little remains to support another level, so chains have three or four steps.
Answer: So much energy is lost at each level that little is left for higher levels
quiz.mistake: Does not link chain length to energy loss

quiz.q: About what percentage of the sunlight falling on leaves do green plants capture?
quiz.explain: Green plants convert about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves into food energy.
steps: Green plants capture only a small part of the sunlight falling on leaves.
From the lesson: about 1%.
So the answer is 1.
Answer: 1
quiz.mistake: Confuses this with the 10 percent law

quiz.q: Why is the flow of energy in an ecosystem called unidirectional?
options: Energy goes back to the Sun
Energy moves from plants to herbivores to carnivores and never returns to the previous level
quiz.explain: Energy captured by producers moves up the levels and is not passed back; nutrients, unlike energy, are recycled by decomposers.
steps: Energy moves from plants → herbivores → carnivores.
It is never passed back to an earlier level or to the Sun.
So energy flow is one-way (unidirectional).
Answer: Energy moves from plants to herbivores to carnivores and never returns to the previous level
quiz.mistake: Confuses the flow of energy with the cycling of nutrients

quiz.q: Which is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
quiz.explain: Abiotic factors are non-living: temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals.
steps: Abiotic components are non-living factors: temperature, rainfall, wind, soil.
Earthworms, bacteria and grass are living (biotic).
So temperature is abiotic.
Answer: Temperature
quiz.mistake: Thinks tiny living things are abiotic

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'If the lion eats deer, why aren't there as many lions as deer in the forest?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Only about 10% of energy passes up each trophic level, so there's only enough for a few lions!
teach.nudge: Good! How much of the energy passes on from one level to the next?

revise.summary: An ecosystem is the living and non-living parts of an area working together. Energy flows one way along food chains from producers to consumers, and only about 10% passes to each next level, so food chains are short.
focus: Tell biotic from abiotic components and natural from artificial ecosystems
Assign trophic levels in a food chain and explain food webs
Use the 10 percent law to calculate energy at each level
remember: Producers → herbivores (primary consumers) → small carnivores → large carnivores
Plants capture about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves
10 percent law: about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level
Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) return nutrients to the soil
traps: Energy flow is unidirectional; it is not recycled like nutrients
Don't count the lion as the 4th level in grass → deer → lion; it is the 3rd
Crop fields and aquariums are artificial ecosystems

learn.hook: High above us, a thin blanket of a special form of oxygen acts like sunscreen for the whole planet!
points: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule of three oxygen atoms. At higher levels of the atmosphere it shields the Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the Sun, which can cause skin cancer in humans.
Ozone forms when UV radiation splits oxygen molecules: O₂ → O + O; then a free oxygen atom joins an oxygen molecule: O + O₂ → O₃.
Ozone is useful high in the atmosphere, but at ground level it is a deadly poison.
The amount of ozone began to drop sharply in the 1980s. This was linked to synthetic chemicals called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) got countries to agree to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels. Today, CFC-free refrigerators are mandatory throughout the world.

example.q: Think it through: why should old refrigerators and ACs be handed over to proper recyclers rather than broken open in a scrapyard?
steps: Older refrigerators and ACs may contain CFC refrigerants.
If released, CFCs rise and damage the ozone layer.
A thinner ozone layer lets more harmful UV radiation reach the Earth.
example.answer: To stop any CFCs inside from escaping and damaging the ozone layer.

learn.reallife: India is one of the many countries that has phased out the production of CFCs under international agreements, so new fridges and ACs sold today are CFC-free.

games.title: How ozone forms high in the atmosphere
items: UV radiation from the Sun reaches the upper atmosphere
UV splits an oxygen molecule (O₂) into two free oxygen atoms
A free oxygen atom combines with an O₂ molecule

games.title: Ozone true or false
items: Ozone is made of three oxygen atoms.
Ozone at ground level is good for breathing.
At ground level ozone is a deadly poison.
The ozone layer protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
It absorbs harmful UV rays from the Sun.
CFCs are used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
These synthetic chemicals were linked to ozone depletion.
The UNEP agreement of 1987 aimed to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels.
It was a global step to protect the ozone layer.
Ozone depletion was first noticed in the 1880s.
The sharp drop in ozone was found in the 1980s.

quiz.q: What is the chemical formula of ozone?
quiz.explain: Ozone has three oxygen atoms in each molecule.
steps: Ozone is made of three oxygen atoms.
So its formula is O₃.
O₂ is ordinary oxygen.
Answer: O₃
quiz.mistake: Confuses ozone with ordinary oxygen

quiz.q: What does the ozone layer protect us from?
quiz.explain: Ozone shields the Earth's surface from harmful UV radiation, which can cause skin cancer.
steps: The ozone layer is high in the atmosphere.
It shields the Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the Sun.
So it protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
Answer: Ultraviolet radiation
quiz.mistake: Thinks ozone blocks all sunlight

quiz.q: Which chemicals are mainly linked to the depletion of the ozone layer?
quiz.explain: CFCs, used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers, damage the ozone layer.
steps: The sharp drop in ozone was linked to synthetic chemicals.
These are chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.
So the chemicals are CFCs.
Answer: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
quiz.mistake: Confuses ozone depletion with global warming

quiz.q: Which reaction shows ozone forming in the upper atmosphere?
quiz.explain: UV splits O₂ into free oxygen atoms; each atom combines with O₂ to form O₃.
steps: UV radiation splits oxygen: O₂ → O + O.
A free oxygen atom joins an oxygen molecule: O + O₂ → O₃.
So the reaction is O + O₂ → O₃.
Answer: O + O₂ → O₃
quiz.mistake: Picks the breakdown of ozone instead of its formation

quiz.q: In which year did UNEP succeed in forging an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels?
quiz.explain: The agreement was reached in 1987.
steps: From the lesson: UNEP got countries to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels.
This agreement was reached in 1987.
So the year is 1987.
Answer: 1987
quiz.mistake: Confuses the agreement year with the base year 1986

quiz.q: Ozone near the ground is —
quiz.explain: Ozone is protective in the upper atmosphere but poisonous at ground level.
steps: High in the atmosphere, ozone protects us from UV.
At ground level ozone is a deadly poison.
So ozone near the ground is a deadly poison.
Answer: A deadly poison
quiz.mistake: Thinks ozone is good everywhere

quiz.q: When did the amount of ozone in the atmosphere begin to drop sharply?
quiz.explain: Scientists noticed the sharp drop in the 1980s and linked it to CFCs.
steps: Scientists noticed a sharp drop in ozone in the 1980s.
It was linked to CFCs.
So the drop began in the 1980s.
Answer: In the 1980s
quiz.mistake: Guesses a much earlier date

quiz.q: Which step helps protect the ozone layer?
options: Using more fire extinguishers with CFCs
quiz.explain: Avoiding CFCs reduces ozone depletion; CFC-free refrigerators are now mandatory worldwide.
steps: CFCs damage the ozone layer.
Avoiding CFCs protects it; CFC-free refrigerators are now mandatory.
Burning plastic and cutting trees do not protect ozone.
So using CFC-free refrigerators helps.
Answer: Using CFC-free refrigerators
quiz.mistake: Mixes up general pollution steps with ozone protection

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'People say there's a hole in the sky's sunscreen! What is the ozone layer and what is damaging it?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Ozone blocks harmful UV rays, and CFCs from old fridges damage it — so we use CFC-free ones!
teach.nudge: Good! Which chemicals are mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer?

revise.summary: Ozone (O₃) high in the atmosphere shields the Earth from harmful UV radiation. It began to fall sharply in the 1980s because of CFCs, and in 1987 UNEP got countries to freeze CFC production.
focus: Explain how ozone forms and why it is useful high up but harmful at ground level
Name the cause of ozone depletion and its effects
Know the steps taken to protect the ozone layer
remember: Ozone = O₃; formed by O₂ → O + O, then O + O₂ → O₃
Ozone layer blocks UV radiation, which can cause skin cancer
1987: UNEP agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels
traps: Ground-level ozone is poisonous, not helpful
CFCs, not carbon dioxide, are the main cause of ozone depletion
The agreement year is 1987; the freeze was at 1986 levels

learn.hook: Peels in a compost pit become rich soil, but a plastic bag thrown today may still be around when you are a grandparent!
points: Biodegradable substances (vegetable peels, leaves, paper, cotton) are broken down by biological processes such as the action of bacteria and fungi.
Non-biodegradable substances (most plastics, glass, some pesticides) are not broken down by these processes. They persist for a long time and can harm living things in the ecosystem.

Biological magnification: non-biodegradable chemicals like some pesticides enter the food chain and are not broken down or excreted, so they build up at each trophic level. Humans, at the top of many food chains, can end up with the highest concentration.

Managing waste: segregate wet (biodegradable) and dry waste at home, compost kitchen waste, reduce single-use plastic, reuse items like glass jars and cloth bags, and send paper, plastic and metal for recycling.
Even 'natural' choices need thought: replacing materials on a very large scale can create new problems, so the best solution is often to reduce waste in the first place.

example.q: Think it through: a pesticide sprayed on crops is found at a higher concentration in fish-eating birds than in the water of the nearby lake. Why?
steps: The pesticide is non-biodegradable, so it is not broken down.
Small organisms absorb it; fish eat many of them; birds eat many fish.
At each level the chemical is stored and accumulates, increasing in concentration.
example.answer: Biological magnification: the chemical builds up at each higher trophic level.

learn.reallife: Many Indian cities ask households to keep separate bins for wet and dry waste so that kitchen waste can be composted and dry waste recycled.

items.text: Substances broken down by bacteria and fungi are called ___.
Build-up of harmful chemicals along a food chain is called biological ___.
The highest concentration of such chemicals is usually found at the ___ trophic level.
Kitchen waste can be turned into manure by ___.

quiz.q: Which of these is non-biodegradable?
quiz.explain: Polythene is not broken down by bacteria or fungi and persists in the environment.
steps: Biodegradable: broken down by bacteria and fungi (peels, paper, cotton).
Polythene (a plastic) is not broken down by them.
So polythene is non-biodegradable.
Answer: Polythene
quiz.mistake: Thinks all household waste rots

quiz.q: What is biological magnification?
options: Increase in the number of organisms at higher levels
Increase in concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals at successive trophic levels
Breaking down of waste by bacteria
quiz.explain: Chemicals that are not broken down accumulate as they pass up the food chain.
steps: Some chemicals are not broken down or excreted.
As they pass up the food chain, they build up at each trophic level.
This rise in concentration at successive levels is biological magnification.
Answer: Increase in concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals at successive trophic levels
quiz.mistake: Confuses magnification with growth in numbers

quiz.q: In the food chain plankton → small fish → large fish → fish-eating bird, where will a non-biodegradable pesticide be most concentrated?
quiz.explain: It accumulates at each level, so the top consumer has the highest concentration.
steps: A non-biodegradable pesticide accumulates at each level.
The highest level here is the fish-eating bird.
So it has the highest concentration.
Answer: Fish-eating bird
quiz.mistake: Thinks the chemical is highest where it first enters

quiz.q: Why are biodegradable substances less harmful to the environment?
options: They are broken down by bacteria and fungi into simpler substances
quiz.explain: Decomposers break them down, returning nutrients to the soil instead of piling up.
steps: Bacteria and fungi break biodegradable substances into simpler substances.
These return nutrients to the soil instead of piling up.
So they are less harmful because decomposers break them down.
Answer: They are broken down by bacteria and fungi into simpler substances
quiz.mistake: Thinks biodegradable means it lasts forever

quiz.q: Which is the best first step for managing waste at home?
options: Mixing all waste in one bag
quiz.explain: Segregation lets wet waste be composted and dry waste be recycled.
steps: Segregating wet and dry waste is the first step.
Wet waste can then be composted and dry waste recycled.
Mixing, burning or dumping waste causes harm.
So segregate wet and dry waste.
Answer: Segregating wet and dry waste
quiz.mistake: Thinks burning waste is a safe solution

quiz.q: Which agents break down biodegradable waste?
quiz.explain: Decomposers like bacteria and fungi break down organic matter.
steps: Biodegradable waste is broken down by biological processes.
The agents are decomposers: bacteria and fungi.
So the answer is bacteria and fungi.
Answer: Bacteria and fungi
quiz.mistake: Does not know the role of decomposers

quiz.q: Why do humans often have high levels of some pesticides in their bodies?
options: Humans make pesticides inside their body
Humans are at the top of many food chains, where these chemicals accumulate
Pesticides are in the air only
quiz.explain: Being top consumers, humans receive chemicals that have built up through all lower levels.
steps: Pesticides build up at each higher trophic level (biological magnification).
Humans are at the top of many food chains.
So humans receive the highest concentrations.
Answer: Humans are at the top of many food chains, where these chemicals accumulate
quiz.mistake: Thinks only direct contact causes exposure

quiz.q: Which action reduces non-biodegradable waste?
options: Using a cloth bag for shopping
Throwing away glass jars after one use
quiz.explain: Reusable cloth bags reduce the use of polythene bags.
steps: Non-biodegradable waste includes polythene bags and single-use plastics.
Using a reusable cloth bag cuts down polythene bags.
Single-use cups, wrapping fruit in plastic and throwing away jars increase waste.
So using a cloth bag for shopping reduces it.
Answer: Using a cloth bag for shopping
quiz.mistake: Confuses reducing waste with recycling later

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Why does Dadi keep banana peels for the garden pit but give plastic to the kabadiwala?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Peels are biodegradable and become compost; plastic isn't, so it goes for recycling!
teach.nudge: Good! Why can't plastic go into the compost pit with the peels?

revise.summary: Biodegradable wastes are broken down by bacteria and fungi; non-biodegradable wastes like plastics persist. Some non-biodegradable chemicals build up along food chains (biological magnification), so waste should be segregated, reduced, reused and recycled.
focus: Classify materials as biodegradable or non-biodegradable
Explain biological magnification with a food chain example
Suggest ways to manage household waste
remember: Biodegradable: broken down by bacteria and fungi (peels, paper, cotton)
Biological magnification: concentration of such chemicals rises at each trophic level; top consumers have the most
Segregate wet and dry waste; compost, reduce, reuse, recycle
traps: Biological magnification is about chemical concentration, not number of organisms
The top consumer, not the producer, has the highest pesticide level
Burning plastic is not a safe way to manage waste
